sources.entry: Vesta - Native macOS terminal built on libghostty for running coding agents in parallel. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/vestaterm/Vesta) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Vesta is a native macOS terminal app built on libghostty for running AI coding agents in parallel, with a workspace sidebar, tmux-style sessions, and a scriptable `vesta` CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Vesta is a Swift/AppKit terminal that links GhosttyKit (libghostty) and renders with Ghostty's Metal engine, reading the existing ~/.config/ghostty/config. It adds a flat workspace sidebar where each row is a terminal session rooted at a directory with native splits, plus optional visual groups. Shells run under a small daemon (vestad) so they survive quitting Vesta and reattach on relaunch, with prefix-key (ctrl+b) mode for tmux-style control. Workspace cards show output tails and success/failure heat driven by OSC 133 marks, and the vesta CLI drives and reads the live UI over a Unix socket so agents can orchestrate panes. It also includes a command palette, in-app and macOS notifications, drag-and-drop of file paths, and a self-updater.
use_cases: run multiple AI coding agents side by side in one window
keep terminal sessions alive after quitting the app
script a terminal from another agent or shell via a CLI
organize project shells into a sidebar with groups and colors
tmux-style split panes on macOS without tmux
get notified when a background command or agent needs attention
notable: Uses real libghostty (GhosttyKit.xcframework) rather than a fork, and reads existing ghostty config and themes
Persistent sessions via a daemon (vestad) that holds PTYs and replays recent output on reattach
Scriptable `vesta` CLI over a Unix socket for agent orchestration, including broadcast send-keys
Workspace cards show output tails and OSC 133-based success/failure heat, Claude Code-aware
Cold restore rebuilds workspace layout and cwd after a reboot, with optional on-disk scrollback
caveats: Requires macOS and an Apple Silicon-style build path (arm64 build directory shown in examples)
Persistent scrollback is written to disk and may contain secrets; it can be disabled with vesta-persist-scrollback = false
Shells survive only window-close or quit; closing panes or workspaces kills their shells
